propositions: A one-time backfill script must sample historical commits (default monthly cadence), measure cyclomatic complexity via lizard and clone counts via jscpd at each commit, and write snapshots with integer-typed complexity and clone_count values.
Each written snapshot must be timestamped with the sampled commit's committer date (ISO format from git show), not the backfill wall-clock time, so the trend timeline is historically accurate.
If a measurement tool is absent or errors on a commit, that commit is skipped and logged without aborting the backfill; other sampled commits continue to be processed and written.
All backfilled snapshots must carry metadata source="snapshot" and confidence="high" to indicate deterministic tool output.

The measurement logic is isolated in a single measure_tree(tree_path) function that returns a dict with complexity and clone_count integers, enabling test monkeypatching without requiring external tools to be installed.
